The issue in the provided code is that when appending a value to the list `A`, the code appends the command type `c` instead of the value `d`. This causes the list to be filled with `1`s instead of the actual values provided in the queries.

Q = int(input())
A = []

for i in range(Q):
  c, d = map(int, input().split())
  
  if c == 1:
    A.append(c)
